subject: MSA — customer IP / third-party indemnity: scope & defense control
messages:

Subject: MSA: indemnity — third-party IP concerns

Diego,

FintechCo legal reviewed the MSA and flagged the indemnity section. Their core asks: Redwood to indemnify and defend FintechCo for third-party claims alleging infringement arising from the Service (including model outputs). They also want:
- Defense and settlement costs, including attorneys' fees.
- No material cap specifically for IP indemnity (they typically carve IP out from liability caps).
- Carveouts only for infringement caused solely by Customer-configured changes or Customer-submitted content.

We attached a comment matrix with suggested language (FintechCo_indemnity_requests.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood's position — especially around: (a) whether we accept uncapped IP indemnity, (b) defense control vs. customer participation, and (c) carveouts for open source / pre-existing models.

Also looping in Mark from procurement to keep timelines in view — we are trying to close the Order Form this month.

Thanks,
Amelia

---

Subject: RE: MSA: indemnity — third-party IP concerns

Diego / Priyom —

Reviewed FintechCo's asks. Proposed positions below (summary for sales):

1) Scope of indemnity
- Redwood will indemnify and defend Customer for third-party claims that the Service as delivered by Redwood infringes a third party's patents, copyrights or trade secrets.
- Exclusions: (i) claims arising from Customer Content (data, prompts, code) or configurations provided by Customer; (ii) claims arising from Customer modifications to the Service; (iii) claims based on open-source components used by Customer or provided to Customer separately.

2) Defense and settlement control
- Redwood requests primary defense control but will permit Customer reasonable participation at Customer's expense.
- Redwood will not enter into settlements that impose ongoing obligations or admit liability on the Customer without Customer's consent.

3) Notice / cooperation
- Standard notice obligation: Customer must promptly notify Redwood in writing of any claim and reasonably cooperate in defense. Failure to timely notify that prejudices Redwood may limit coverage.

4) Cap
- Recommend a compromise: treat IP indemnity as subject to a separate cap tied to the annual Order Form value (e.g., 3x annual fees) or a fixed amount (we should discuss $5M as starting point). Given sales timing pressure, a capped exposure helps keep underwriting predictable.

5) Attorneys' fees and costs
- Redwood will cover reasonable costs of defense; need to be explicit that Redwood covers attorneys' fees incurred in defense it controls.

6) Patent-specific carveouts
- We should try to narrow to literal infringement by the Service (not claims based on model outputs that are probabilistic or third-party model behavior).

Attached: preliminary redline language and a short comment matrix.

If sales wants a softer stance on defense control we can allow Customer to control non-binding settlement proposals for de minimis amounts, but not material settlements.

Lauren
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RDW_MSA_redline_for_FintechCo_v2.docx]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: MSA: indemnity — third-party IP concerns

Thanks Lauren — useful summary. Two sales asks:
1) Defense control: FintechCo will push hard to control defense; can we make the language: "Redwood shall have the right to assume defense, provided that Customer may participate at its own expense and Redwood shall not settle any claim that imposes liability on Customer without Customer's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld)" — that softer "not to be unreasonably withheld" language usually closes deals faster.
2) Cap: FintechCo will ask for no cap on IP. They are strategic — if we can offer $5M instead of an absolute carveout it may be fine. Would like Laurel/Finance to ok $5M as a floor.

Goal: close by end of month. Can legal give a near-final that we can send to Amelia by tomorrow morning?

—Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Stone <amelia.stone@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA: indemnity — third-party IP concerns

Amelia — appreciate the patience. Attached is a proposed compromise redline (RDW_MSA_redline_for_FintechCo_v2.docx) and a short note on each change. Summary of Redwood's proposal:

- Redwood will indemnify and defend Customer against third-party claims alleging the Service as delivered infringes a third party's IP rights (patent, copyright, trade secret).
- Excluded from Redwood's indemnity: claims arising solely from (a) Customer Content (including prompts and datasets provided by Customer), (b) Customer modifications or derivative works created by Customer, and (c) components that are governed by separate open-source licenses that were provided directly to Customer.
- Defense control: Redwood will have the right to assume and control the defense. Customer may participate at its own expense. Redwood will not settle any claim that imposes material obligations or admissions of liability on Customer without Customer's written consent (consent not to be unreasonably withheld).
- Cap: Redwood proposes a specific cap for IP indemnity equal to the greater of (i) three times the annual fees for the Order Form, or (ii) USD 5,000,000. We can surface pricing concessions if the customer insists on removing the cap, but need executive approval.
- Attorneys' fees: Redwood will pay reasonable attorneys' fees as part of the covered defense when Redwood controls defense.

We hope this preserves the customer's protection while keeping risk bounded for Redwood. If FintechCo can accept the above in principle, we can send a clean redline for signature and start DocuSign for the Order Form.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Diego Fernandez
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Diego / Lauren — thanks for the thoughtful compromise. A few quick points from our side:

1) Defense control is acceptable provided Redwood commits to timely updates and that any settlement that would require ongoing performance or admission of liability by FintechCo requires explicit FintechCo sign-off (we agree to "not unreasonably withhold" consent).
2) Attorneys' fees: please confirm Redwood's indemnity explicitly includes reasonable attorneys' fees and costs of defense.
3) Cap: FintechCo prefers no cap for IP claims; if Redwood cannot remove it, we will accept USD 10,000,000 as a compromise.

If Redwood can accept the above (confirm attorneys' fees language and raise cap to $10M or remove cap), we will proceed to sign the Order Form ASAP. Otherwise, we will need to escalate.

Amelia
